# Coding-agent behavior reference

_A maintained reference to the coding-agent differences discern must handle: hooks, sandboxes, working-directory and session semantics, worktree mechanisms, Model Context Protocol (MCP) client behavior, and configuration surfaces. It gives maintainers one evidence-backed place to answer why agents behave differently._

> **What this is.** A cross-agent comparison compiled in mid-2026 from vendor documentation, issue trackers, and one agent's tool schemas through a fan-out research pass. It covers Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor agent CLI, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI. An “—” or “unverified” cell lacks a pinned source and remains open for later research.
>
> **Companion.** [Agent integration coverage](agent-integration-coverage.md) records what discern wires for each agent: the Instruction file, Skills directory, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and worktree hooks. This page records the vendor capabilities that coverage cites.
>
> **How this grows.** Each behavioral dimension owns a section, and each agent owns a column. Add a row when evidence shows a divergence. Cite the source and state the confidence. This page serves maintainers and coding agents.
>
> **Freshness.** Flags, defaults, and tool surfaces change between releases. Most behaviors are pinned to mid-2026. MCP schema discovery was re-verified on 2026-08-02 against Claude Code 2.1.212, Codex `rust-v0.146.0`, Cursor's current documentation, Gemini CLI v0.53.1, and Copilot CLI 1.0.77. MCP result-field delivery was re-verified on 2026-08-14 using the sources named in §11. Re-verify a cell before relying on it as current.

The matrix supports these cross-cutting conclusions.

**Mid-session re-root.** Claude Code and GitHub Copilot can re-root a running session into a worktree mid-conversation (Claude's `EnterWorktree`; Copilot's `/cwd` and `/worktree`). **Codex, Cursor, and Gemini pin the working or workspace root at launch** and require a fresh session to move it. On those launch-pinned agents, a human or orchestrator starts the fresh session when an agent on the trunk needs an isolated worktree.

**Committed configuration and trust.** Codex forbids self-trust from repository configuration. Cursor needs `--trust` in print mode. Gemini ignores project `.gemini/settings.json` (hooks, MCP, and `.env`) in safe mode until the folder is user-trusted. Copilot stores trust in a user-level `trustedFolders` list. A committed hook or MCP entry is therefore inert on a fresh clone for those agents. **Claude Code honors committed project configuration without a separate trust step.** Instruction files remain readable regardless of trust: Gemini reads `GEMINI.md` in safe mode, and the others read `AGENTS.md`. That makes the author-once → compiled-file pipeline the integration surface that works before a trust grant.

**Convergent instruction surfaces.** Codex, Cursor, Gemini, and Copilot read the cross-tool `.agents/skills/`; Claude Code uses `.claude/skills/` (#31005). Codex, Cursor, and Copilot also read `AGENTS.md` natively. A compiled `AGENTS.md` and a materialized `.agents/skills/` cover those shared surfaces. Claude Code needs `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills/`; Gemini needs `GEMINI.md`. A `@AGENTS.md` pointer supplies the agent-specific instruction files.

## 1. Pre-execution interception (block-before-run)

Each researched agent exposes a hook that fires before a tool call and can block it. Committed project configuration wires the hook to an external binary. The hooks use a common form (JSON on stdin and exit 2 or a deny response to block) with different schemas, events, and reliability.

- **Claude Code** — `PreToolUse` (in `.claude/settings.json`). Receives `tool_name`, `tool_input` (incl. `command`), `cwd`. Blocks via exit 2 or `{permissionDecision: "deny"}`. Caveat: reportedly **not fired on subagent tool calls** (`anthropics/claude-code#21460`). A separate `CwdChanged` hook fires _after_ a `cd` (observational only).
- **OpenAI Codex CLI** — `PreToolUse` (in `[hooks]` / `hooks.json` under `~/.codex` or `<repo>/.codex`). Same payload shape. Maintainer framing: **"a guardrail, not an enforcement boundary"** — it "doesn't intercept all shell calls yet, only the simple ones." A separate `notify` channel exists but fires only on turn-complete and cannot block.
- **Cursor agent CLI** — `beforeShellExecution` (in `.cursor/hooks.json`). Receives `command`, `cwd`, `workspace_roots`. Blocks via `{permission: "deny"}` or exit 2. The CLI honors the hook, although reports say that the CLI fires only a subset of the documented events as of 2026-04. `.cursor/cli.json` permissions are static lists with no callback or cwd scoping.
- **Gemini CLI** — `BeforeTool` (in the `hooks` key of `settings.json`, merged across `~/.gemini/` and project `.gemini/`). Receives `tool_name`, `tool_input`, optional `mcp_context`, plus base fields (`session_id`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, …). Blocks via stdout `{"decision":"deny"}` (alias `"block"`) with a required `reason` surfaced to the agent as a tool error, or exit 2 with the reason on stderr. Version 0.36.0 added an `"ask"` decision. The hook runs synchronously. Project `.gemini/settings.json` remains inactive in safe mode until the folder has a user trust grant, so a committed hook does not activate itself on clone.
- **GitHub Copilot CLI** — `preToolUse` (in `.github/hooks/*.json`, `~/.copilot/hooks/`, or inline in `.github/copilot/settings.json`). Reads a JSON stdin payload (`sessionId`, `cwd`, `toolName`, `toolArgs`) and writes JSON to stdout; blocks via `permissionDecision: "deny"` (with a required `permissionDecisionReason`). The most strict of the set: it is **fail-closed** — any error, crash, timeout, or non-zero exit on `preToolUse` _denies_ the call. Approval prompts (`--allow-tool`/`--deny-tool`) are a separate, non-programmable layer.

**Implication.** The interception logic can live once in a shared binary, with thin per-agent adapters translating schemas and verdicts. Each researched agent has a blocking pre-execution hook. These hooks do not provide a hard enforcement boundary against an evasive agent. Claude Code has open reports in which `permissionDecision: "deny"` is ignored and the tool runs (`anthropics/claude-code#37210`, `#4669`, `#19298`). Those reports concern deny-path reliability. Copilot's fail-closed default denies a call after any hook error, crash, timeout, or nonzero exit.

## 2. Tool-input rewriting and result substitution

- **Rewrite the command before execution:** Claude Code and Codex support an `updatedInput` channel that mutates `tool_input.command` and runs the modified command. Permissions are checked again afterward. Use one authoritative rewriting hook per tool to avoid nondeterministic last-writer-wins behavior. Gemini's `BeforeTool` returns `hookSpecificOutput.tool_input`, which merges with and overrides the model's arguments before execution. Copilot's `preToolUse` returns `modifiedArgs` to substitute tool arguments. Cursor's `beforeShellExecution` output is permission-only (`permission`, `user_message`, and `agent_message`) and has no command-mutation field. Cursor can change MCP output after execution through `postToolUse.updated_mcp_tool_output`.
- **Substitute the result:** A Claude Code denial surfaces to the model as an error. Cursor's pre-execution hook is permission-only, Codex's hook is approve or deny, Gemini's `BeforeTool` has no synthetic-output field, and Copilot's `preToolUse` allows, denies, or rewrites. Gemini can replace a result after execution through `AfterTool.tailToolCallRequest`, and Copilot can replace one through `postToolUse.modifiedResult` (`{resultType, textResultForLlm}`). Gemini's `BeforeModel.llm_response` can also mock the model reply. None of these hooks can block real execution and return synthetic success at the pre-execution point. A hook can redirect a command, such as by wrapping it in a sandbox CLI, but cannot transparently run the command elsewhere and return the output.

## 3. Native OS sandbox

|                                      | Claude Code                                                    | Codex                                                                                                                                                                         | Cursor                                                                       | Gemini                                                                                         | GitHub Copilot                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Toggle                               | `sandbox.enabled` (off by default)                             | `sandbox_mode` (`workspace-write` etc.; default on)                                                                                                                           | `.cursor/sandbox.json`; CLI **without a sandbox unless `--sandbox enabled`** | `-s`/`--sandbox`, `GEMINI_SANDBOX`, `tools.sandbox` (off by default; auto-on under `--yolo`)   | `/sandbox enable` + `sandbox` key in `settings.json` (off by default)                                      |
| Writable-root → arbitrary dir        | `filesystem.allowWrite`                                        | `[sandbox_workspace_write].writable_roots` / `--add-dir`                                                                                                                      | `workspace_readwrite` + `additionalReadwritePaths`                           | workspace dir writable + `SANDBOX_MOUNTS` (`from:to:opts`, default `ro`)                       | working dir auto read/write; manually added paths                                                          |
| Back ends                            | Seatbelt / bubblewrap+socat                                    | Seatbelt / bubblewrap+seccomp                                                                                                                                                 | Seatbelt / Landlock+seccomp+overlayfs / WSL2                                 | Seatbelt (macOS) / Docker·Podman·runsc·lxc (Linux) / native integrity-level (Windows, v0.36.0) | Microsoft MXC, cross-OS (per-OS implementation names undocumented)                                         |
| Network default                      | off; domain allowlist via proxy                                | off in workspace-write                                                                                                                                                        | `deny`; domain allow/deny lists                                              | **allowed** under default `permissive-open` profile                                            | configurable (`allowedHosts`/`blockedHosts` "not reliable across platforms"); shipped default undocumented |
| **Linked-worktree `.git` carve-out** | **automatic** (allows shared `.git`, denies `hooks/`+`config`) | **none — actively hostile**: resolves the `.git` pointer's `gitdir:` and forces the _resolved_ common-dir read-only, so worktree commits fail (`openai/codex#7071`, `#15505`) | not handled (must add the common-dir to writable roots)                      | unverified (no `.git`/common-dir carve-out documented)                                         | unverified (no git-aware rule documented)                                                                  |
| Fail mode if unavailable             | warn + run without a sandbox (`failIfUnavailable` to harden)   | fails closed (refuses / asks)                                                                                                                                                 | n/a                                                                          | n/a (off by default)                                                                           | n/a (off by default)                                                                                       |

The carve-out row determines whether Git commits work inside a linked worktree. Claude Code's native sandbox accounts for commits that write into the shared `.git` directory outside the worktree. Codex resolves the relocated common directory and forces it read-only, so `git commit` fails inside a sandboxed linked worktree. Cursor leaves the common directory unhandled. Gemini, Copilot, and the external wrappers `fence` and `srt` do not document a carve-out. discern must compute and inject the carve-out for every mechanism except Claude Code's native sandbox.

## 4. Sandbox nesting / composition

An agent's native operating-system (OS) sandbox can conflict with an external wrapper such as `fence` or `srt` during Linux namespace creation. Configure one OS-sandbox mechanism per agent: the native sandbox or an outer launch wrapper. The following controls determine whether the native sandbox can be disabled:

- **Claude Code — no off-switch.** It exposes no flag to disable its sandbox in favor of an outer layer, so the native sandbox is the available composable option.
- **Codex — yes.** `--sandbox danger-full-access` (or `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, documented for use "inside an externally hardened environment") disables it — that phrasing is itself the sanctioned compose-with-a-wrapper story.
- **Cursor — yes.** `sandbox.json` `"type": "insecure_none"` disables the sandbox entirely (at the cost of reverting to per-command approval).
- **Gemini — yes, by default.** The native sandbox is off unless opted into, and `security.toolSandboxing: false` disables tool isolation (docs note this does not address process-level isolation, so full nesting semantics are unverified).
- **Copilot — yes, by default.** The sandbox is off until `/sandbox enable`, and `/sandbox disable` turns it off again — so an outer wrapper can be the only mechanism with no fight.

Codex, Cursor, Gemini, and Copilot can use an outer wrapper as their single mechanism. Claude Code requires its native sandbox.

## 5. Working-directory persistence across tool calls

- **Claude Code** — **persists.** A `cd` in one Bash call carries to the next (the working directory is durable session state; only shell env/functions reset). So a single `cd` moves the shell for the rest of the session.
- **Codex** — **does not persist.** Each shell or exec call runs in its own subshell and takes an explicit `workdir`. OpenAI's prompting guide says “Do not use `cd`.” The launch cwd (`--cd`) supplies a per-call default that the model can override. The writable-root sandbox provides confinement.
- **Cursor** — **does not persist.** The Shell Mode docs state "each command runs independently — use `cd <dir> && …`"; every command re-anchors to the CLI working directory.
- **Gemini** — **does not persist.** `run_shell_command` takes a per-call `dir_path` (absolute, or relative to workspace root); to work elsewhere you pass `dir_path` each call or chain `cd … && …`. A persistent `/cd` is an open, not-yet-implemented request (`google-gemini/gemini-cli#25020`).
- **Copilot** — **unverified at the per-call level.** The _session_ working dir is settable mid-session (`/cwd`, `/cd`), but whether a `cd` inside one shell tool call carries to the next is not documented. Treat as non-persistent until confirmed.

## 6. Mid-session re-root (move the working / project root of a _running_ session)

Claude Code and GitHub Copilot can re-root a running session. Codex, Cursor, and Gemini keep the root pinned at launch.

- **Claude Code — yes.** The built-in **`EnterWorktree`** tool "switches the current session into" a worktree, and with `path` can enter an _existing_ worktree that appears in `git worktree list` (which sibling worktrees do, from a non-worktree session). It re-roots cwd and re-resolves CWD-dependent state (CLAUDE.md, memory, plans). `ExitWorktree` will **not** remove a worktree entered by `path`, so an external owner such as discern keeps lifecycle control. Caveat: its _special_ cases (already in a worktree, or a pinned subagent) require the target be under `.claude/worktrees/`, which collides with a sibling-placement convention; the base "from the main checkout" case is unaffected. (Sourced from the live `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tool schemas.)
- **GitHub Copilot — yes.** A running session can change its working dir without restart via **`/cwd`** (alias `/cd`, "show or change working directory"), and **`/worktree`** (alias `/move`) re-roots the session into a new worktree, carrying uncommitted changes along. So, like Claude Code, Copilot can both create and _inhabit_ a worktree in-session.
- **Codex — no.** The working and writable root is fixed at launch. The documented switch sequence is exit → `cd` → `codex resume` (`openai/codex#12464`). If the launch directory disappears mid-session, the app reports **“Current working directory missing”** and refuses further input without an in-session recovery. The behavior reproduces when any directory under a live session is renamed or removed and appears in several open issues. A `discern_accept` call from a Codex session inside its own `environment.toml`-managed worktree lands the change and then removes the session's cwd, locking the session on the next message. Launch Codex in the **main checkout** and run `discern_start` there. Sibling worktrees can then be removed while the session's main-checkout cwd remains available through acceptance and the next task.
- **Cursor — no.** Workspace root is pinned at launch through `--workspace` or cwd. The `--worktree` flag redirects edits while leaving the session root pinned.
- **Gemini — no.** Root is pinned at launch. The “switch root mid-session” request is **closed as not planned** (`google-gemini/gemini-cli#18055`). `/directory add <path>` can widen the workspace at runtime while leaving the project root unchanged. The native `--worktree` flag acts at launch.

**Consequence for an agent on the trunk that needs a worktree mid-session:** Claude Code can use `create` and `EnterWorktree`, and Copilot can use `/worktree`. Codex, Cursor, and Gemini can create a worktree from the running session but require a fresh session to work inside it. A human or orchestrator starts that session with `codex --cd <wt>`, `agent --workspace <wt>`, or `gemini --worktree …`; Gemini's command creates the worktree at launch.

## 7. MCP server root mobility

A project-scoped MCP server is a persistent subprocess rooted at its launch directory. In **Claude Code**, a mid-session `cd` or `EnterWorktree` moves the shell and cwd-dependent caches while the running MCP server remains rooted at launch. MCP tools that resolve the project root therefore keep targeting the launch directory. The project's CLI can rediscover the root from cwd on each call. Restarting the session is the supported client-side way to re-root the server. **Copilot** can move cwd through `/cwd` or `/worktree`; whether its running stdio MCP server follows remains undocumented and unverified. **Codex, Cursor, and Gemini** cannot move cwd mid-session. Gemini also gives each MCP server a static per-server `cwd` at launch.

This behavior was confirmed in mid-2026 with discern's stdio MCP server (`discern mcp`), which resolves its project root from the process cwd at spawn. A session opened in a worktree makes `discern_status` return `location: "worktree"`; a session opened in the main checkout keeps returning `location: "main"` after `cd` or `EnterWorktree`. A main-rooted session that calls `discern_start` likewise leaves its process-rooted tools on main. An integration that needs its MCP surface to follow the agent within one session must hold and update a logical target root itself.

> **Resolved in discern by [ADR 0062](../../_adr/0062-mcp-server-working-root.md).** The `discern mcp` server holds a mutable logical working root and re-aims it on `discern_start` (to the new worktree) and `discern_accept` (to the spawn root). The process cwd stays pinned at spawn, while discern's tools follow the recorded logical root. The agent must move its file-operation cwd into the worktree.

## 8. Worktree, launch, trust, and file surfaces

The committed-config and launch surfaces discern must target, one table per dimension. (Where a cell concerns the agent CLI specifically, that is the surface described; IDE/coding-agent deltas are noted inline.)

### Worktree mechanism

| Agent              | Mechanism                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools (own worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`), `--worktree`, and a `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` **hook contract** for version-control-system (VCS) agnostic isolation. discern can drive its lifecycle hook.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | The Codex **app** manages git worktrees in `$CODEX_HOME/worktrees` (Local-vs-Worktree mode; `.worktreeinclude` copies git-ignored files); the bare CLI has no `--worktree` flag yet (manual `git worktree` works). A committable `<repo>/.codex/environments/environment.toml` carries **`[setup].script`** (runs on worktree creation — a `WorktreeCreate` analogue) **and `[cleanup].script`** (runs on worktree teardown when the thread is archived/evicted — a `WorktreeRemove` analogue), both scoped to app-managed worktrees. The closed-source Desktop app generates the schema (capture exact keys from the file); cleanup-on-archive has an open reliability bug (`openai/codex#19480`). |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `-w`/`--worktree [name]` → `~/.cursor/worktrees/<repo>/<name>`; auto-cleaned by the editor's retention rules; **no create/remove hook**. Separate cloud background-agent concept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Gemini CLI         | Native `--worktree`/`-w` (v0.36.0, experimental, behind `experimental.worktrees`): `git worktree add` + branch on launch; **create-only** (no auto-remove/`prune`); **no hook contract**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | Native `/worktree` (alias `/move`): creates a worktree, switches the session into it, carries uncommitted changes; **no create/remove hook**, **no auto-cleanup** (manual `git worktree remove`). (VS Code has a separate session-setup "worktree isolation" UI.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Claude Code exposes an explicit, VCS-agnostic `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hook contract that discern can drive. Codex's `environment.toml` fires committable `[setup]` and `[cleanup]` scripts for Codex-managed worktrees. Each agent has a committable `SessionStart` hook (§9) that can run per-worktree setup. Teardown reliability varies: Claude's `WorktreeRemove` and Codex's `[cleanup]` are committable remove hooks, with an open Codex bug at `#19480`; Gemini's `SessionEnd` is advisory; Cursor's CLI `sessionEnd` remains unverified; and Copilot's `sessionEnd` fires. A worktree owner should drive creation and removal, point the agent at the worktree through its launch-directory flag, and use `SessionStart` for setup. It can use the full `[setup]` and `[cleanup]` pair for Codex-managed worktrees.

### Launch bound to a directory

| Agent              | Launch-dir flag                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `claude <dir>` / `--worktree`                                                                                   |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `--cd` / `-C` (also `codex exec --cd`)                                                                          |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `--workspace <path>` (or plain cwd)                                                                             |
| Gemini CLI         | `--include-directories` / `context.includeDirectories` (or cwd; `#13669` reports that it is not always honored) |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `-C <dir>` ("change working directory before doing anything else"); `--add-dir` for extra access                |

Each researched agent fixes its workspace or writable root at launch. Claude Code and Copilot can move that root mid-session (§6).

### Self-granting trust from committed config

| Agent              | Can a cloned repo self-trust?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | **n/a** — no separate trust prompt; settings in `.claude/settings.json` (committed or local) are honored directly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | **No** for the trust _grant_ — `trust_level` is a user-level `~/.codex/config.toml` `[projects."<path>"]` key (only the `projects`/`profile` keys are ignored in repo-local config). After a one-time directory trust grant, Codex honors its committed `<repo>/.codex/config.toml` (including `[mcp_servers]`), `.codex/hooks.json`, and `.codex/environments/environment.toml`. |
| Cursor agent CLI   | **No.** Workspace-trust prompt on first run; `--trust` works only with `-p`/`--print` (headless). The interactive terminal user interface (TUI) has no corresponding flag. Cursor honors committed rules, MCP servers, and hooks after trust.                                                                                                                                     |
| Gemini CLI         | **No.** Folder Trust (off by default); in "safe mode" it ignores project `.gemini/settings.json`, `.env`, custom commands, MCP servers, and hooks until user-trusted (prompt / `~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json` / IDE signal / `--skip-trust` / `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`).                                                                                                |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | **No.** Folder-trust prompt; `trustedFolders` stored in user-level `~/.copilot/config.json` (not committable); bypass via `--allow-all*` flags or pre-seeding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Codex, Cursor, Gemini, and Copilot gate committed configuration behind a user-level trust step. Claude Code honors committed project configuration directly. Each agent reads its instruction file before trust, as the next table records.

### Instruction file (auto-loaded; is `AGENTS.md` read?)

| Agent              | Instruction file                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `CLAUDE.md` (supports the `@path` import); does **not** read `AGENTS.md` natively.                                                                                                                                                  |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `AGENTS.md` natively (concatenated; **no** import directive — so it is the canonical full-body file the pointers import).                                                                                                           |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `AGENTS.md` **and** `CLAUDE.md` natively at root (plain Markdown, applied as rules alongside `.cursor/rules/`; nested files, more-specific-wins). `.mdc` rules support `@file` references; full inline behavior remains unverified. |
| Gemini CLI         | `GEMINI.md` by default (key `context.fileName`), with `@file.md` imports; does **not** read `AGENTS.md` unless `context.fileName` lists it (open requests `#12345`/`#10401`/`#4970`).                                               |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `AGENTS.md` natively as **primary** (+ `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`), plus `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (repo-wide) and `.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md` (path-scoped via `applyTo`, additive); **no** `@import`.        |

Codex, Cursor, and Copilot read `AGENTS.md` directly. Claude and Gemini need a per-agent file, and a `@AGENTS.md` pointer satisfies both. Trust-gated agents read this instruction file before trust, so the compiled file works on a fresh clone.

### Skills (Agent Skills / `SKILL.md`)

| Agent              | Skills directory                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `.claude/skills/` **only** — does not read `.agents/skills/` (anthropics/claude-code#31005, open).                                                                                                   |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `.agents/skills/` (its only repo path; not `.codex/skills/`).                                                                                                                                        |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `.agents/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/` (+ `.claude/skills/`, `.codex/skills/` compatibility dirs). CLI loading of skills is IDE-documented and **partial/unverified for the CLI binary** specifically. |
| Gemini CLI         | `.gemini/skills/` or the `.agents/skills/` alias (the alias takes precedence).                                                                                                                       |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` (project); `~/.copilot/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` (personal).                                                                                  |

The researched agents use the same `SKILL.md` folder format in different directories. Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Copilot read the cross-tool `.agents/skills/`, so one materialized copy serves them. Claude Code reads `.claude/skills/` (#31005).

### Config file locations

| Agent              | Config surfaces                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code        | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.mcp.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `~/.codex/config.toml`, `<repo>/.codex/config.toml` (incl. `[mcp_servers]`, inline `[hooks]`), `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`, `<repo>/.codex/environments/environment.toml`, `AGENTS.md`                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `.cursor/` (`rules/`, `mcp.json`, `hooks.json`, `cli.json`, `sandbox.json`), `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; skills in `.agents/skills/` / `.cursor/skills/`                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Gemini CLI         | `settings.json` layered (system-defaults → `~/.gemini/` → project `.gemini/` → system) with `hooks`/`mcpServers`/`tools.sandbox`/`security.*`; `GEMINI.md`                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | user-level `~/.copilot/` (`config.json`, `settings.json`, `mcp-config.json`, `copilot-instructions.md`, `hooks/`, `skills/`); repo-level `.github/` (`copilot-instructions.md`, `instructions/**`, `skills/`, `hooks/*.json`, `copilot/settings.json`) **plus committable `.mcp.json` / `.github/mcp.json`** (CLI MCP, takes precedence over the user-level file), `AGENTS.md` |

## 9. Committable config: MCP and lifecycle hooks

Each researched agent accepts committed MCP configuration and exposes a committable `SessionStart` hook. Trust, approval, and teardown reliability vary by agent.

### MCP config

| Agent              | Committable MCP file                        | Shape                                                                               | Gate                                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `.mcp.json` (project)                       | `mcpServers` map (stdio `command`/`args`)                                           | pre-approved via `enabledMcpjsonServers`; no trust prompt |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `<repo>/.codex/config.toml`                 | `[mcp_servers.<name>]` (`command`/`args`/`env_vars`/`env`/`url`)                    | one-time directory **trust**, then honored                |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `.cursor/mcp.json` (project)                | `mcpServers` map (stdio + SSE + HTTP)                                               | per-tool **approval** + workspace trust                   |
| Gemini CLI         | `.gemini/settings.json` (project)           | `mcpServers` map                                                                    | **Folder Trust** — inert in safe mode until trusted       |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `.mcp.json` or `.github/mcp.json` (project) | `mcpServers` map; **takes precedence over** user-level `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` | folder trust                                              |

Each agent reads a committable project MCP file. Claude pre-approves that file with no trust prompt. Codex and Copilot require a one-time trust grant. Cursor and Gemini require trust and per-tool approval.

### Session lifecycle hooks (setup / teardown)

| Agent              | Start event    | End event                                           | Committable file                                                   | CLI-firing / reliability                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code        | `SessionStart` | `WorktreeRemove` (worktree teardown) + `SessionEnd` | `.claude/settings.json`                                            | fires; the only paired worktree create+remove contract                                                    |
| OpenAI Codex CLI   | `SessionStart` | `[cleanup].script` (env.toml)                       | `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`; `.codex/environments/environment.toml` | `SessionStart` fires; `[cleanup]` runs on worktree archive/eviction (committable; open bug `#19480`)      |
| Cursor agent CLI   | `sessionStart` | `sessionEnd` (present in file)                      | `.cursor/hooks.json`                                               | `sessionStart` fires in `cursor-agent`; **`sessionEnd`-in-CLI unverified**; cloud agents fire neither     |
| Gemini CLI         | `SessionStart` | `SessionEnd`                                        | `.gemini/settings.json` (`hooks`)                                  | fires, but `SessionEnd` is **"advisory"** (not guaranteed on crash); both regressed on v0.24.0 (`#16697`) |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `sessionStart` | `sessionEnd`                                        | `.github/hooks/*.json`                                             | both fire in the CLI ("all hook events … supported by the CLI")                                           |

Each agent gives discern a committable hook for setup at session or worktree start. Teardown reliability and scope vary. Claude Code provides `WorktreeRemove`. Codex provides an `environment.toml` `[cleanup].script` for Codex-managed worktree archives, with an open reliability bug at `#19480`. Copilot's CLI `sessionEnd` fires, Gemini's event is advisory, and Cursor's CLI firing remains unverified. Reliable teardown also requires out-of-band reclamation, which discern performs through a `prune` sweep.

## 10. MCP schema discovery and startup loading

MCP itself does not define deferred tool schemas. A `tools/list` result carries each tool's full definition, and the core `Tool` shape permits implementation-specific `_meta`; neither the protocol nor its schema defines `defer_loading` or `alwaysLoad` behavior. Deferral is a client-and-model context policy layered over that response.

Protocol discovery and model exposure are separate. Every client below can call `tools/list` at startup while withholding some or all returned schemas from the model until a later search. The relevant parity question asks which tools the model can select before that search. A client may already know the server's inventory.

| Client                    | Default model exposure                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Per-tool eager control                 | Whole-server or global control                                                                                                                                              | Evidence and limits                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code               | Tool Search begins with names and server instructions; schemas are deferred.                                                                                                                                              | `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"] = true` | Server entry `"alwaysLoad": true`; `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` disables search globally.                                                                                     | Tool and instruction text is bounded at 2KB. Server control applies to every transport from 2.1.121. High confidence: documented client contract.                                                                      |
| OpenAI Codex              | The client calls `tools/list`; when the model and provider support Tool Search, every allowed MCP tool is registered as deferred and found through `tool_search`. Otherwise schemas are direct.                           | None                                   | None. `enabled_tools` and `disabled_tools` remove tools rather than changing exposure. Historical Tool Search feature keys are accepted only as ignored compatibility keys. | The first 512 instruction characters should be self-contained and become search-namespace context. High confidence: official docs and released open-source core. CLI, IDE, and app share that core and project config. |
| Cursor IDE and agent CLI  | Dynamic context discovery starts with a small static inventory including tool names; details are read when needed. The CLI likewise says it loads MCP tools only when needed.                                             | None documented                        | None documented. `/mcp enable` and disable change availability only.                                                                                                        | High confidence in lazy exposure from Cursor's docs; medium confidence in the absence of an override because the client is closed-source and its complete config schema is not published.                              |
| Gemini CLI                | Every enabled MCP tool is registered after `tools/list`, and all active function declarations are sent with model requests.                                                                                               | None needed or supported               | None. `includeTools` and `excludeTools` change availability only.                                                                                                           | Eager exposure is the fixed default: it already loads every server tool in advance, but cannot represent a request to defer. High confidence: official docs and open-source client.                                    |
| GitHub Copilot CLI        | On supported models, Tool Search activates when the session has roughly 30 or more tools; built-ins stay direct and MCP/external tools are deferred. Below the threshold, or on unsupported models, all tools are direct. | None                                   | Per-server `"deferTools": "never"`; user-level `"toolSearch": false` disables deferral globally.                                                                            | High confidence: official CLI docs. `deferTools` shipped in 1.0.63.                                                                                                                                                    |
| GitHub Copilot in VS Code | Tool Search keeps a core set of about 30 tools direct and defers MCP tools on supported models.                                                                                                                           | None documented                        | No MCP-server field is documented; model-specific Tool Search settings are global.                                                                                          | High confidence in dynamic exposure; medium confidence in the absence of a server override because the surface is not open-source.                                                                                     |

Claude Code and Copilot CLI share `.mcp.json`, so their different keys raise an interoperability question. Direct parser checks against Claude Code 2.1.212 and Copilot CLI 1.0.77 found that an entry containing both `"alwaysLoad": true` and `"deferTools": "never"` is accepted. Each client applies its own field and discards the other without a diagnostic. This behavior is version-specific. MCP does not guarantee it, and neither client promises to preserve the foreign key if it rewrites the file. VS Code remains unverified; its current MCP configuration reference documents neither property, so its schema diagnostics may reject or flag them even if the runtime is tolerant.

The controls therefore do not form a portable boolean:

- Claude Code can eagerly expose one tool or one server.
- Copilot CLI can eagerly expose a server. It has no per-tool control, and its key and value differ from Claude Code's.
- Gemini already exposes every enabled schema and cannot defer them.
- Codex and Cursor provide no supported server-originated eager override.

An `always_load` project setting could mean “request eager exposure where the client supports it.” `true` could map to Claude Code and Copilot CLI and be an already-satisfied no-op for Gemini. Codex and Cursor have no corresponding control, and `false` cannot make Gemini defer. This best-effort preference has provider-specific gaps. Availability allowlists do not replace it because they make the remaining lifecycle tools unreachable.

**discern decision, 2026-08-03.** Keep the portable server contract in its returned definitions and put the gateway and lifecycle at the start of `instructions`; Codex's 512-character instructions makes that ordering useful beyond Claude Code's 2KB bound. Do not expose a public `[mcp]` setting or emit per-tool Anthropic metadata. For evaluation only, `DISCERN_EXPERIMENTAL_MCP_PRELOAD=1` maps the configured providers into the shared entry: `alwaysLoad: true` for Claude Code and `deferTools: "never"` for Copilot. The default output remains unchanged, and no mapping is attempted for Codex, Cursor, or Gemini. This environment-only seam can be removed or promoted if provider support converges.

## 11. How clients deliver result fields to the model

An MCP `tools/call` result may carry content blocks in `content` and a JSON object in `structuredContent`. The protocol recommends serializing structured results into a text content block for backward compatibility. It does not define which fields a client places in model context. The researched clients apply different policies:

| Client surface     | Model-facing behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Other surface or limit                                                                                                                                   | Evidence and confidence                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code        | A July 2026 reproduction using Agent SDK 0.3.220 and its bundled Claude Code 2.1.211 found that a present `structuredContent` object becomes the serialized model-facing `tool_result` and replaces the `content` blocks.           | The same report found raw structured data reattached after the oversize-result persistence path had replaced the normalized content with a file pointer. | Medium confidence: a reproducible report plus extracted bundled code, with no documented stability contract. |
| OpenAI Codex       | The open-source model-sanitization path retains `content` and `structured_content` in the returned `CallToolResult`.                                                                                                                | A separate event copy used for storage and UI collapses an oversize aggregate result into a text preview, clearing `structured_content` and `_meta`.     | High confidence: current open-source core.                                                                   |
| Cursor             | Cursor support states that the serialized tool result sent to the model includes `structuredContent`. The response does not document precedence when `content` is also present.                                                     | `afterMCPExecution` currently serializes `content` and `isError`, omitting `structuredContent`.                                                          | Medium confidence: a vendor support response for a closed-source client.                                     |
| Gemini CLI         | `transformMcpContentToParts` reads `response.content` to build `llmContent` and has no `structuredContent` path. A missing or malformed `content` array becomes a parse-error message.                                              | The human display conversion also reads `content`.                                                                                                       | High confidence: current open-source client path.                                                            |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | Since 1.0.56, the CLI surfaces human-readable `content` and `structuredContent` to the agent. It deduplicates text that is the literal JSON serialization of the structured object; otherwise, it concatenates the representations. | Earlier releases could drop one representation. Earlier release notes covered structured-content display without specifying a model-facing contract.     | High confidence: the vendor changelog states the agent-facing policy and the release that introduced it.     |

These facts are specific to the cited releases and surfaces. MCP does not promise how an agent host constructs model context. A portable server contract must assume that either field may be the only model-facing representation. Each representation therefore needs the state, blockers, authority boundaries, and next action required for correct continuation. Keep their combined size bounded because Codex and Copilot can forward each field. Cursor's hook path also shows that one client can expose different fields to its model and automation surfaces.

A probe server can place distinct sentinels in the 2 fields and update this matrix for a pinned client version. The probe cannot establish behavior for future releases.

## 12. MCP tool-call duration

MCP defines cancellation and progress messages, but it does not impose one tool-call timeout. Each client supplies its own request policy:

| Client surface          | Total-request behavior                                                                                                                                                                                            | Configuration and published maximum                                                                                                                                               | Progress behavior                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code             | `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` defaults to 100,000,000 ms (about 28 hours). Network transports also begin with a 60-second per-request bound; raising the environment or per-server value above 60 seconds raises that bound. | Environment-wide `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` or per-server `timeout`. No maximum is published. Separate idle windows default to five minutes for network servers and 30 minutes for stdio. | Progress resets the separate idle window; the total execution timeout still applies. |
| OpenAI Codex CLI        | Per-tool default is 60 seconds.                                                                                                                                                                                   | `mcp_servers.<id>.tool_timeout_sec`. No maximum is published.                                                                                                                     | Unpublished.                                                                         |
| Cursor Agent CLI / ACP  | Current CLI build `2026.07.23-e383d2b` uses a 60,000 ms bound. Cursor calls the bundled software development kit (SDK) with no request options, so the SDK's default becomes the effective fixed bound.           | No supported per-server timeout setting. The 60 seconds remains the SDK default because the client supplies no override.                                                          | `resetTimeoutOnProgress` remains false, so progress does not renew the timer.        |
| Cursor editor IDE Agent | Cursor support reports around 60 minutes. A May 2026 support statement put the IDE on the CLI's 60-second path; the July statement supersedes that duration.                                                      | No precise maximum or supported per-server timeout is published. Agents Window and cloud-agent limits remain unverified.                                                          | Current behavior is unverified.                                                      |
| Gemini CLI              | Default is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).                                                                                                                                                                               | Per-server `timeout` in milliseconds. No maximum is published.                                                                                                                    | Unpublished.                                                                         |
| GitHub Copilot CLI      | No default is published.                                                                                                                                                                                          | Per-server `timeout` in milliseconds. No maximum is published.                                                                                                                    | Unpublished.                                                                         |

The [MCP TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/client.md#timeouts) supplies a 60-second default and lets clients override both the duration and `resetTimeoutOnProgress`. Cursor Agent CLI leaves both at their defaults. Cursor support confirmed the resulting [CLI/ACP limit and the longer path in the IDE](https://forum.cursor.com/t/agent-acp-mcp-tools-call-times-out-at-60s-with-no-way-to-configure-it/163925/5). A source audit of the official Darwin ARM64 CLI package produced SHA-256 `f2eb25851f2079dcdf0558a816e06c402d187abfca93255d35167020439ebbf2` for build `2026.07.23-e383d2b`; its `McpSdkClient.callTool` supplies no request options, while the bundled SDK resolves `timeout` with `?? 6e4` and `resetTimeoutOnProgress` with `?? false`.

Cursor is therefore two timeout domains. The project-local `.cursor/mcp.json` is shared by its IDE and CLI, and the client identifiers observed on the wire are not a published capability contract. An integration that needs one generated entry for both uses the CLI-compatible bound or requires an explicit user choice. A long-running operation should return resumable state before that bound; progress alone cannot keep the CLI/ACP request alive.
